approach.method_basis: The Parent alternates direct neural molecular proposals with two graph refinement phases. It learns from a full archive of real accepted scores and exact molecular token trajectories sampled by score rank. Joint trajectory-balance updates adapt the policy and a learned normalizer, while policy-to-prior categorical KL keeps a reference to frozen corpus-trained weights. A fingerprint Gaussian posterior allocates graph-offspring evaluations and protects the initial fresh-policy handoff. The frozen prior was selected along unchanged unlabeled training by valid, connected, unique generation yield, with original holdout loss breaking ties. In its current update, both trajectory-specific score mismatch and the common normalizer mismatch contribute to policy credit.
approach.novelty: Center the trajectory-balance policy credit within each actual replay minibatch and assign the common mismatch to the existing normalizer alone. Each trajectory still receives relative credit from its exact accepted score and likelihood, and every pairwise difference in those coefficients is retained. Unlike the earlier scaffold mixture or reversed KL penalty, this changes neither which records are learned from nor the reference distribution. It tests whether separating shared normalization error from relative policy learning makes accepted-score adaptation more useful; it does not assume that zero mean credit or lower loss guarantees better molecules.

hypothesis: Center accepted trajectory-balance policy coefficients within each replay minibatch while routing the detached common residual exclusively to the learned normalizer, preserving score-ranked replay and the original categorical prior penalty.

finding_summary.headline: Centering activated, but common error grew and useful neural emission fell
finding_summary.insights:
The common policy-credit component was not merely an expendable normalization error in this setting. Removing it left the scalar objective unchanged at a given state, yet shifted much more unresolved error onto the normalizer and weakened later transfer of graph feedback into neural proposals. This happened while graph-origin replay share increased from 73.54% to 75.43%, so dilution of graph records is not the explanation. Greater emitted scaffold variety and the disappearance of duplicate raw draws also failed to compensate for lower valid yield and policy-origin scores.

The early-versus-late reversal narrows the problem to continuing accepted-score adaptation rather than a different prepared prior: the checkpoint identities and preparation were unchanged. Preserving the direct normalizer derivative was insufficient to preserve its trajectory, because the policy state and shared clipping changed. The improved sitagliptin endpoint must also be read alongside the molecular assessment, which found prominent peroxide-linked, stereochemically undefined structures; broader graph coverage does not establish better chemical quality. Mechanism execution is confirmed, while the registered search-advantage condition is unsupported. The remaining question is how to control common and relative learning jointly without discarding the useful molecular transfer observed in the parent.
finding_summary.results:
All 7,200 replay updates used the intended centered policy credit. Independent differentiation verified that the common term had no policy gradient and that the normalizer retained its original direct derivative. The change reversed 99,068 of 230,400 policy-credit signs while preserving pairwise differences and the scalar loss value within numerical precision. Nevertheless, the common mismatch became much larger in the resulting histories: its mean squared contribution was 44.130, compared with 4.418 in the parent, accounting for 62.59% rather than 14.95% of trajectory-balance loss.

Raw valid novel yield fell from 7,991/12,000 draws (66.59%) to 6,861/12,280 (55.87%). The first adapted policy batches improved in validity, but later yield fell from 64.00% to 51.82%. Mean accepted policy-origin score fell from 0.204941 to 0.172874, and later emitted molecules matching previously trained graph scaffolds fell from 53 to 15. The three-seed mean final score fell from 0.550198 to 0.542654, a decrease of 0.007543; paired changes were -0.009239, -0.029845 and +0.016454. All fifteen task replicas completed their 300 evaluations.

molecular.headline: Recognizable amide and piperazine chemistry is mixed with acid chlorides, N-O-O chains and stereochemically undefined polycycles
molecular.overall_character: The supplied panel is complete: each of five tasks has 900 evaluated molecules across three seeds, including 870 optimizer proposals. All 4,350 optimizer-proposal SMILES parse with RDKit. Rings and aromatic atoms are plentiful: digest ring-closure rates are 0.9851-0.9931 and aromatic-token rates 0.9402-0.9828. In fixed task order, proposal median heavy-atom counts are 25, 37, 25, 30 and 26, and median ring counts are three, five, three, four and four. Conventional aryl propionamides, aminoheteroaryls, cyclic tertiary amines, arylsulfonylpiperazines and aromatic dicarbonyl systems coexist with O-fluoro groups, O-acyl hydroxylamines, acid chlorides, bridged sulfur/nitrogen ring systems and unusual N-O-O-C substituents. These liabilities occur in leading families: one task contains 139 acid-halide proposals; another contains 211 proposals with O-O single bonds, including 201 with N-O-O chains, and its highest structure has seven RDKit-perceived unassigned stereocentres. No proposal assigns a stereocentre, while counts containing an unassigned centre are 492, 198, 389, 350 and 538. Each task has 553-679 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds, but leading molecules repeat close families rather than establish broad accessible synthetic diversity. The parent already generated elaborate ring systems and unusual bonds; current acid-halide and peroxide-rich families make those limitations prominent. Overall drug-likeness is weak because major leading families carry reactive or physically burdensome features, despite conventional amide and piperazine subsets. The trajectories do not establish synthesis or stable experimental compounds.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule is an alpha-aryl propionamide whose amide nitrogen carries a methylene-linked N-arylpyrrole; the attached aryl group is a fluoropyridine. It has 25 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings and an unassigned alpha-carbon stereocentre. Related leaders use pyrazoles, an O-acyl hydroxylamine connection instead of the amide, or ring-contracted unsaturated nitrogen heterocycles. The ordinary amides are recognizable medicinal chemistry; aryl O-F, acyl-O-N and four-membered unsaturated nitrogen-ring variants need separate qualification. Parent leaders included indole-amide and fused heterocyclic structures, whereas this digest concentrates around a three-ring propionamide/heteroarylmethyl architecture.
liabilities: An O-acyl hydroxylamine is an acyl-O-N connection, chemically distinct from an ordinary amide or hydroxamic acid; the score does not establish its stability.
Sixteen proposals contain O-halogen bonds and 23 N-halogen bonds, although the highest displayed molecule requires neither.
Eleven proposals have at most three heavy atoms and 18 exceed 50, so fragmentation and overgrowth coexist with the leading ring-rich chemistry.
missing_features: The leading alpha-aryl acyl family does not specify its central stereocentre, leaving the proposed configurations undefined.
Broad stable alternatives retaining the useful amide/heteroaromatic relationship are less visible than O-F, N-O and small-ring variants.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The conventional amide scores 0.445826 and its displayed aryl O-F counterpart 0.445454, showing tolerance rather than a demonstrated need for O-fluorination. In another local pair, an O-acyl hydroxylamine scores 0.442718 and the direct amide 0.432360; that extra oxygen changes bond chemistry, not just polarity. A related three-ring amide remains at 0.417399, whereas truncated two-ring amide or heteroaryl structures score 0.007181 and 0.004449. Very large assemblies and tiny halogen or hydrazine species reach zero. The visible association is a particular moderate-size ring/linker/carbonyl arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The highest family is a three-ring aminoheteroaryl assembly with methoxy, dimethylamino, bromo or fluoro substituents and a vinyl-ether-containing N-substituent. Its top member has 34 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings and molecular mass 534.390. A second leading family has arylsulfonamide/anilino frameworks bearing two acid chlorides, often with methylenedioxy and sulfur/nitrogen fused rings. These are recognizable reactive intermediates rather than demonstrated stable final medicinal compounds. Some variants add aromatic bridges or unusual sulfur double-bond arrangements. Full proposals have median 37 heavy atoms, five rings and molecular mass 573.860; 201 exceed 50 heavy atoms. Acid-halide proposals increase from 15 in the parent to 139 here.
liabilities: There are 139 acid-halide proposals, and several leaders contain two acid chlorides, providing reactive acylating sites rather than demonstrated persistent drug-like substituents.
Thirty-three proposals contain O-halogen bonds and 41 have O-O single bonds, distinct concerns from ordinary aryl halogenation.
The proposal range reaches 111 heavy atoms and molecular mass 2035.098, limiting the practical meaning of graph validity.
missing_features: Stable functional-group alternatives retaining the useful polar/aromatic arrangement are not demonstrated across the high-score acid-chloride neighborhood.
The output lacks consistently economical whole-molecule coverage around the aminoheteroaryl family, often extending into larger repeated or fused structures.
Synthetic access and stable geometry are unestablished for the aromatic bridges and unusual sulfur-bond variants.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aminoheteroaryl leader scores 0.615282, a close analogue 0.614174 and a methoxy-for-bromo variant 0.613310, so bromine is not required for a nearby score. The bis-acid-chloride sulfonamide scores 0.613582; ring-bridged or sulfur-bond variants remain near 0.61. Those values tolerate reactive groups without establishing chemical persistence. Replacing methoxy with O-F in a local aminoheteroaryl pair gives 0.609781 versus 0.614174, providing no benefit from O-F. Low sulfone-rich or heavily elaborated structures lie around 0.285-0.299 despite many rings and heteroatoms.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule combines a nine-membered tertiary-amine ring with indole and phenol regions, an ethyl substituent and a fluoromethylamino arm. It has 32 heavy atoms, four rings and two unassigned stereocentres. The fluoromethylamino arm is N-CH2-F, not a direct N-F bond. Eight-membered analogues, bridged amines, dimethylaminoethyl aromatic frameworks and aldehyde-bearing arylpiperidines also lead. These include familiar medicinal motifs, but medium or bridged rings raise synthetic and conformational questions. Parent leaders likewise combined cyclic amines with aromatic, indole or phenolic regions; the current digest emphasizes medium-size rings and unusual junctions. Full proposals have median 25 heavy atoms and three rings.
liabilities: Eight- and nine-membered rings and multiple bridges impose conformational and synthetic questions that the graphs do not resolve.
Some leaders contain aldehydes, and 32 proposals have direct N-halogen bonds; the highest N-CH2-F structure must not be confused with those direct N-F species.
Sixteen proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, with a maximum of 95, showing excessive elaboration around otherwise useful amine chemistry.
missing_features: Leading medium-ring and bridged amines lack explicit relative configurations and established conformations; 389 proposals contain unassigned stereocentres.
No additional mandatory group follows from near-ceiling scores; economical stable alternatives preserving the observed amine/aromatic relationships are the supported need.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The nine-membered amine scores 0.999991, an eight-membered analogue 0.997059, a less elaborate dimethylaminoethyl aromatic structure 0.993803 and an aldehyde-bearing arylpiperidine 0.993765. Their shared feature is accessible amine functionality positioned with aromatic regions; the nine-membered ring and fluoromethylamino arm are not universal requirements. Low acylhydrazone, carbamate, thiosemicarbazone and amide examples lie near 4.11e-05 to 1.11e-04 despite nitrogen and rings. A terminal direct N-F cyclic amine scores 0.247498 while other terminal amines remain above 0.91, but those are different structures and do not isolate an N-F substituent effect.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest family is conventional arylsulfonylpiperazine chemistry with the second piperazine nitrogen attached to a substituted quinoline-like or diazaaromatic fused ring. The highest has 29 heavy atoms, four rings, three aromatic rings and molecular mass 409.555. Methyl, fluoromethyl, chlorine, hydroxyl and amino substitutions supply close alternatives. Another leader is a fused aromatic dicarbonyl nitrogen heterocycle attached to an ethoxy-substituted N/O ring system. These leaders are more chemically straightforward than many terminal structures. The parent also produced sulfonamide and fused cyclic-carbonyl architectures. Current proposals have median 30 heavy atoms and four rings versus parent medians of 32 and four, with 666 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds.
liabilities: Sulfonylated and aryl-attached piperazine nitrogens are electronically different from interchangeable free aliphatic amines.
Terminal proposals include O-O-containing rings, dense sulfur/nitrogen fusion and duplicated carbonyl frameworks without established stability or synthetic access.
Sixty-eight proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, substantially larger than the leading conventional piperazines.
missing_features: Useful sulfonylpiperazine and dicarbonyl arrangements have limited distinct alternatives beyond local substitutions with identical or nearly identical scores.
The wider output lacks consistent ring-fusion and configurational control: 350 proposals have unassigned centres, although the highest piperazine family is achiral.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The arylsulfonylpiperazine scores 0.232655, the alternative dicarbonyl compound 0.231883 and the fluoromethyl variant 0.231824. Several amino, hydroxyl, fluoro or aryl-halogen variants share 0.225523, giving little evidence that more peripheral decoration resolves the remaining gap. Small ethane, ether, carbonate or guanidine-like species score approximately 0.012-0.029 and lack the combined aromatic/polar-ring architecture. Terminal examples repeating carbonyl heterocycles or adding complex rings remain around 0.139-0.203. More ring closure or heteroatoms alone therefore does not explain the useful arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The highest family combines a five-membered lactone or cyclic carbamate with a multiply fluorinated fused sulfur/nitrogen system and a fluorinated cyclopropyl group. Most displayed members also carry an unusual N-O-O-C connection. The highest has 29 heavy atoms, five rings, only one aromatic ring and seven RDKit-perceived unassigned stereocentres. This is detailed connectivity without configurational specification, and the N-O-O chain combines N-O and peroxide bonds. Another high family contains an N-fluoro sulfur-containing fused system; terminal molecules show nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl cores linked to unsaturated sulfur rings bearing carbon allenes. Parent leaders also included unusual fluorinated heterocycles, but current O-O proposals rise from 48 to 211, including 201 with N-O-O chains. These structures need strong chemical qualification as stable compounds.
liabilities: N-O-O chains occur in 201 proposals and any O-O single bond in 211; these are chemically different from ordinary ethers or amino substituents.
Twenty-five proposals contain N-halogen bonds and 29 carbon allenes; 19 place an allene in a perceived ring of at most seven atoms, leaving local reactivity and ring geometry unresolved.
Several cited lactone/carbamate leaders have five to seven unassigned centres, so saturated complexity does not establish a coherent specified stereoisomer.
missing_features: Stable alternatives preserving the useful carbonyl, fluorinated-ring and nitrogen arrangement without N-O-O chains or other unusual bonds are not demonstrated across the leading neighborhood.
The highest structure has seven unassigned centres, and 538 proposals contain unassigned centres with none assigning any; defined three-dimensional molecules are missing.
Stable geometry and synthetic access are unestablished for fused sulfur/nitrogen cores, fluorinated small rings and cyclic-allene alternatives.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The lactone/N-O-O structure scores 0.519276 and a ring-connectivity analogue 0.501405. In a close cyclic-carbamate pair, the N-O-O version scores 0.492253 and its shorter N-O counterpart 0.463156. That numerically favors peroxide insertion in this pair without establishing stability. A different N-fluoro fused structure scores 0.475223. Several terminal carbon-allene sulfur-ring compounds reach approximately 0.302-0.403. Very polar glycosylated, multiply hydroxylated or oversized structures are as low as 1.13e-128. The full median is 0.0028918204 and there are no exact-zero rows, so this is a wide score distribution rather than a zero-score population.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One set contains 139 acid halides and leaders with two acid chlorides near score 0.613. Another has 211 O-O proposals, 201 with N-O-O chains; a cyclic-carbamate pair scores 0.492253 with N-O-O versus 0.463156 with N-O. Elsewhere, ordinary amide and aryl O-F variants score 0.445826 and 0.445454, showing that the reactive bond is not numerically needed in that pair. All structures pass RDKit parsing, which does not establish chemical persistence.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably distinguish stable functional-group alternatives from reactive connections tolerated by scores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide stable bonds and functional groups that preserve useful observed arrangements. Distinguish amides from O-acyl hydroxylamines, ethers from peroxide or N-O-O chains, aryl halogens from O-halogen bonds, and stable carbonyl groups from acid halides independently of objective identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: No assigned stereocentres occur in 4,350 optimizer proposals. The five sessions contain 492, 198, 389, 350 and 538 proposals with unassigned centres. The highest peroxide-bearing lactone has seven RDKit-perceived unassigned centres, and leading propionamides and medium-ring amines also omit configuration. Several strong piperazines are achiral, so the issue is conditional.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator adds stereogenic complexity without defining the configurations of its proposed molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support explicit chemically consistent configurations and relevant bond geometries when the structure permits them, while retaining achiral alternatives. Complex connectivity must not substitute for specified three-dimensional molecules, and the data do not prescribe an unobserved preferred stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The five sessions contain 18, 201, 16, 68 and eleven proposals above 50 heavy atoms; the largest has 111 heavy atoms and molecular mass 2035.098. High-score aminoheteroaryls also include simpler three-ring structures, and conventional four-ring sulfonylpiperazines score above more elaborate terminal carbonyl assemblies. Other proposals contract aromatic heterocycles into small unsaturated rings or create medium and bridged amine rings without defining geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent control of molecular growth and ring elaboration around useful chemical arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain economical alternatives with controlled linker length, topology, appendage count and mass while preserving useful polar relationships. Overgrowth and indiscriminate ring contraction can both lose valuable chemistry; the missing capability is contextual control of accessible whole molecules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each task has 553-679 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds, yet leaders cluster around propionamides, aminoheteroaryls, bis-acid-chloride sulfonamides, medium-ring amines, sulfonylpiperazines or fluorinated peroxide-bearing polycycles. Several piperazine amino, hydroxyl, fluoro and aryl-halogen variants share 0.225523. In an aminoheteroaryl family, bromo and methoxy alternatives remain near 0.614 while O-F substitution is lower than its methoxy counterpart.
transferable_gaps.gap: Substantial graph diversity still produces narrow leading families and repetitive peripheral-substitution alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Broaden meaningful core and linker alternatives preserving useful functionality, beyond repeated halogen swaps and ring closures. Functional-group position, electronic environment and stable geometry need representation alongside scaffold identity, with their usefulness determined by observed feedback.

method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

research_intent.falsifier: The mechanism is falsified if a nonzero shared residual still appears in the actual policy coefficients, their sum is nonzero beyond roundoff, the detached common normalizer term contributes a policy gradient, pairwise coefficient differences change, or the direct normalizer gradient before clipping differs from the inherited 2*mean(raw residual). Equal scalar loss values alone do not establish activation. If centering activates but graph-bearing displacement, useful emission or complete-panel score benefit does not improve, the proposed search advantage remains unsupported. Changed replay selection, original KL direction, labels, preparation or frozen graph/posterior components constitute a contract failure.
research_intent.implementation_change: Change only trajectory-balance gradient routing in the active accepted_feedback_flow_policy Layer. For the actual inherited minibatch of B accepted trajectories let d_i=logP_i-logR_i, z=logZ and c=stop_gradient(mean_i d_i). Compute centered policy terms (d_i-c)^2 and the normalizer-only term (z+c)^2. The optimized scalar is mean_i[(d_i-c)^2 + inherited_KL_coefficient*KL(policy||frozen_prior)_i] + (z+c)^2. Thus its TB numerical value equals the inherited mean_i[(z+d_i)^2] up to roundoff, but its policy log-likelihood coefficients are 2*(d_i-c)/B and its direct normalizer gradient remains 2*(z+c), exactly the inherited batch-mean residual gradient at the same state. Mechanism execution is confirmed, while the registered search-advantage condition is unsupported. molecular_assessment.headline: Recognizable amide and piperazine chemistry is mixed with acid chlorides, N-O-O chains and stereochemically undefined polycycles
molecular_assessment.overall_character: The supplied panel is complete: each of five tasks has 900 evaluated molecules across three seeds, including 870 optimizer proposals. All 4,350 optimizer-proposal SMILES parse with RDKit. Rings and aromatic atoms are plentiful: digest ring-closure rates are 0.9851-0.9931 and aromatic-token rates 0.9402-0.9828. In fixed task order, proposal median heavy-atom counts are 25, 37, 25, 30 and 26, and median ring counts are three, five, three, four and four. Conventional aryl propionamides, aminoheteroaryls, cyclic tertiary amines, arylsulfonylpiperazines and aromatic dicarbonyl systems coexist with O-fluoro groups, O-acyl hydroxylamines, acid chlorides, bridged sulfur/nitrogen ring systems and unusual N-O-O-C substituents. These liabilities occur in leading families: one task contains 139 acid-halide proposals; another contains 211 proposals with O-O single bonds, including 201 with N-O-O chains, and its highest structure has seven RDKit-perceived unassigned stereocentres. No proposal assigns a stereocentre, while counts containing an unassigned centre are 492, 198, 389, 350 and 538. Each task has 553-679 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds, but leading molecules repeat close families rather than establish broad accessible synthetic diversity. The parent already generated elaborate ring systems and unusual bonds; current acid-halide and peroxide-rich families make those limitations prominent. Overall drug-likeness is weak because major leading families carry reactive or physically burdensome features, despite conventional amide and piperazine subsets. The trajectories do not establish synthesis or stable experimental compounds.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule is an alpha-aryl propionamide whose amide nitrogen carries a methylene-linked N-arylpyrrole; the attached aryl group is a fluoropyridine. It has 25 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings and an unassigned alpha-carbon stereocentre. Related leaders use pyrazoles, an O-acyl hydroxylamine connection instead of the amide, or ring-contracted unsaturated nitrogen heterocycles. The ordinary amides are recognizable medicinal chemistry; aryl O-F, acyl-O-N and four-membered unsaturated nitrogen-ring variants need separate qualification. Parent leaders included indole-amide and fused heterocyclic structures, whereas this digest concentrates around a three-ring propionamide/heteroarylmethyl architecture.
liabilities: An O-acyl hydroxylamine is an acyl-O-N connection, chemically distinct from an ordinary amide or hydroxamic acid; the score does not establish its stability.
Sixteen proposals contain O-halogen bonds and 23 N-halogen bonds, although the highest displayed molecule requires neither.
Eleven proposals have at most three heavy atoms and 18 exceed 50, so fragmentation and overgrowth coexist with the leading ring-rich chemistry.
missing_features: The leading alpha-aryl acyl family does not specify its central stereocentre, leaving the proposed configurations undefined.
Broad stable alternatives retaining the useful amide/heteroaromatic relationship are less visible than O-F, N-O and small-ring variants.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One set contains 139 acid halides and leaders with two acid chlorides near score 0.613. Another has 211 O-O proposals, 201 with N-O-O chains; a cyclic-carbamate pair scores 0.492253 with N-O-O versus 0.463156 with N-O. Elsewhere, ordinary amide and aryl O-F variants score 0.445826 and 0.445454, showing that the reactive bond is not numerically needed in that pair. All structures pass RDKit parsing, which does not establish chemical persistence.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably distinguish stable functional-group alternatives from reactive connections tolerated by scores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide stable bonds and functional groups that preserve useful observed arrangements. Distinguish amides from O-acyl hydroxylamines, ethers from peroxide or N-O-O chains, aryl halogens from O-halogen bonds, and stable carbonyl groups from acid halides independently of objective identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: No assigned stereocentres occur in 4,350 optimizer proposals. The five sessions contain 492, 198, 389, 350 and 538 proposals with unassigned centres. The highest peroxide-bearing lactone has seven RDKit-perceived unassigned centres, and leading propionamides and medium-ring amines also omit configuration. Several strong piperazines are achiral, so the issue is conditional.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator adds stereogenic complexity without defining the configurations of its proposed molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support explicit chemically consistent configurations and relevant bond geometries when the structure permits them, while retaining achiral alternatives. Complex connectivity must not substitute for specified three-dimensional molecules, and the data do not prescribe an unobserved preferred stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The five sessions contain 18, 201, 16, 68 and eleven proposals above 50 heavy atoms; the largest has 111 heavy atoms and molecular mass 2035.098. High-score aminoheteroaryls also include simpler three-ring structures, and conventional four-ring sulfonylpiperazines score above more elaborate terminal carbonyl assemblies. Other proposals contract aromatic heterocycles into small unsaturated rings or create medium and bridged amine rings without defining geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent control of molecular growth and ring elaboration around useful chemical arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain economical alternatives with controlled linker length, topology, appendage count and mass while preserving useful polar relationships. Overgrowth and indiscriminate ring contraction can both lose valuable chemistry; the missing capability is contextual control of accessible whole molecules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each task has 553-679 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds, yet leaders cluster around propionamides, aminoheteroaryls, bis-acid-chloride sulfonamides, medium-ring amines, sulfonylpiperazines or fluorinated peroxide-bearing polycycles. Several piperazine amino, hydroxyl, fluoro and aryl-halogen variants share 0.225523. In an aminoheteroaryl family, bromo and methoxy alternatives remain near 0.614 while O-F substitution is lower than its methoxy counterpart.
transferable_gaps.gap: Substantial graph diversity still produces narrow leading families and repetitive peripheral-substitution alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Broaden meaningful core and linker alternatives preserving useful functionality, beyond repeated halogen swaps and ring closures. Functional-group position, electronic environment and stable geometry need representation alongside scaffold identity, with their usefulness determined by observed feedback.

approach.method_basis: The Parent alternates direct neural molecular proposals with two graph refinement phases. It learns from a full archive of real accepted scores and exact molecular token trajectories sampled by score rank. Joint trajectory-balance updates adapt the policy and a learned normalizer, while policy-to-prior categorical KL keeps a reference to frozen corpus-trained weights. A fingerprint Gaussian posterior allocates graph-offspring evaluations and protects the initial fresh-policy handoff. The frozen prior was selected along unchanged unlabeled training by valid, connected, unique generation yield, with original holdout loss breaking ties. In its current update, both trajectory-specific score mismatch and the common normalizer mismatch contribute to policy credit.
approach.novelty: Center the trajectory-balance policy credit within each actual replay minibatch and assign the common mismatch to the existing normalizer alone. Each trajectory still receives relative credit from its exact accepted score and likelihood, and every pairwise difference in those coefficients is retained. Unlike the earlier scaffold mixture or reversed KL penalty, this changes neither which records are learned from nor the reference distribution. It tests whether separating shared normalization error from relative policy learning makes accepted-score adaptation more useful; it does not assume that zero mean credit or lower loss guarantees better molecules.
